nodes.summary: Let $K$ be the Conway knot $11n34$, realized as a closed polyline in $\mathbb{R}^3$ (the braid closure of a 4-strand braid word for it), and let $N$ be its number of vertices. The periodic piecewise-linear parametrization of $K$, which traverses each edge in unit time, is injective on the interval $[0, N)$.
nodes.title: The Conway knot polyline is a simple closed curve

nodes.title: The Conway knot is not smoothly slice (Piccirillo)

nodes.summary: Let $K$ be the PL knot traced by the braid closure on $4$ strands of the braid word $\sigma_1^{-2} \sigma_2 \sigma_1^{-1} \sigma_2 \sigma_1^{-1} \sigma_3 \sigma_2^{-2} \sigma_3^2$ for the Conway knot 11n34. Then $K$ is topologically slice: there is a smooth knot $J$ whose image is unoriented topologically ambient isotopic in $\mathbb{R}^3$ to the image of $K$, and $J$ is topologically slice.
nodes.title: The Conway knot is topologically slice

nodes.summary: There is a PL knot $K$ (a closed polyline in $\mathbb{R}^3$ with at least three vertices, not required to be simple) that is topologically slice but not smoothly slice. can_prove.label: ready to prove
can_prove.meaning: Statement is in Lean and nothing it needs is blocked, so the proof can start.

can_state.label: ready to state
can_state.meaning: Everything its statement uses is in Lean, so the statement can be written in Lean.

conditional.label: conditionally proved
conditional.meaning: Proof compiles, but rests on an open statement without a recorded Lean proof.

fully_proved.label: fully proved
fully_proved.meaning: Proved, and every prerequisite is fully proved too.

inventory_checked.label: inventory checked
inventory_checked.meaning: Module inventory checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

inventory_pending.label: inventory pending
inventory_pending.meaning: Module inventory not yet checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

not_ready.label: not ready
not_ready.meaning: Needs more blueprint work before it can be attempted.

proved.label: proved
proved.meaning: Proof compiles, but something it rests on is not finished.

stated.label: statement formalized
stated.meaning: Statement is in Lean; the proof is not.
